source: independent judge (claude, disposable worktree, no access to the verdict file)
why: Judge verdicts are otherwise written by the same agent that wrote the code. This run exists to produce dissent that self-review structurally cannot.
adjudication: UNADJUDICATED — each FAIL must be verified by hand before it is treated as real, and each one that turns out to be wrong must be recorded as wrong.

verdicts.note: useRuns.ts:52-56 builds the error message from a nested ternary (aborted ? … : err instanceof Error ? … : 'load failed') that has to be decoded to read. KpiStrip.tsx:56-61 is another nested ternary for the average display. useRuns.ts:40-43 picks between `get` and `fetch` with an undefined-check ternary where a default parameter would read at a glance. RunSearch.tsx:55-68 renders a <label style={{display:'none'}}>, which never reaches the accessibility tree, and the input repeats the same text in aria-label. RunSearch.tsx:61 sets role="searchbox" on type="search", which already has that implicit role. The JSDoc at RunSearch.tsx:31 says the query arrives 'already-trimmed, lowercased', yet RunSearch.tsx:35 trims and lowercases it again. RunDetail.tsx:348 and RunDetail.tsx:409 compute the same `title` expression twice.

src/lib/useDrawerA11y.ts:8-17 is a re-export shim with no production caller. MobileDrawer.tsx:5 imports the shared design-system/MobileDrawer directly, and grep shows the shim's only importer is its own test (useDrawerA11y.test.ts:2). It is a test-only dual. Its header says it was kept 'so existing imports and tests are unchanged.' summary.ts:3 re-exports safeHttpUrl and safeUrl. Nothing imports safeHttpUrl from it, and only summary.test.ts:7 imports safeUrl from it, while production code (summary.ts:4) imports safeUrl straight from design-system. The `get` parameter of fetchRuns (useRuns.ts:37) is never passed by its only production caller (useRuns.ts:73), so it is a layer that exists only for tests.

theme.ts:25-26 exposes the shared space and radius tokens, but components hand-roll values instead. KpiStrip.tsx:22 sets borderRadius: 10, and KpiStrip.tsx:23 pads with `theme.space.sm + 2`. RunList.tsx:28-30 sets gap: 10, minHeight: 56 and padding '10px 12px'. RunList.tsx:43-50 hardcodes 36, 36, 9 and 15. RunList.tsx:260 sets minHeight: 32. StatusBadge.tsx:30 sets borderRadius: 999. RunDetail.tsx:258 hardcodes a monospace font stack the theme does not define. linkStyle and recoveryLinkStyle at RunDetail.tsx:68-86 are near-duplicates. The loading and error

markup is repeated in Home.tsx:35-53 and RunDetail.tsx:350-369, with no shared state component. Home.tsx:72 re-implements the trim check that matchesRunQuery already does.

Commit dd9abb6, the latest dashboard fix, bundles at least four unrelated tickets. (1) New vitest browser and VRT lanes: a workspace, dependencies and baseline PNGs. (2) A run-detail feature linking the result file and commit, which touches runLinks.ts, the provenance parsing in summary.ts, and en.ts. (3) Moving the score-note width out of inline style (Home.tsx:68, theme.css). (4) Gate-check changes outside the app: fe-breadcrumbs, fe-resource-links and lib/rendered-detail-id.mjs. The diff is not scoped to one ticket.

dd9abb6 added the .ra-score-note class (Home.tsx:68, theme.css:75) and its 60ch measure, and no assertion covers either: grep of src and tests finds no test that references ra-score-note or scoreNote. Home.test.ts:39-74 covers loading, error, empty and no-match. It never asserts the ready path where a query narrows the list to a non-empty subset, and it never checks that the score note renders. RunList.tsx:243-249 is an empty branch that RunList.test.ts:18-21 asserts, but production cannot reach it because Home.tsx:55 and Home.tsx:72 handle both empty cases first. That test covers dead code, not behaviour. The border colour-mix branch in StatusIcon (RunList.tsx:148-150) has no assertion.

Several e2e assertions check presence, not behaviour. runs.spec.ts:25 checks count > 0, and runs.spec.ts:32-35 checks length > 0 plus that the text contains a digit. runs.spec.ts:51 passes when the first element matching /pass|fail|blocker|rule/i is visible, and nav or chrome text can satisfy that. runs.spec.ts:92 passes when the first link on the page is visible, and the header logo satisfies that. The unit tests have the same weakness. RunList.test.ts:31 checks that the html contains '100', and RunList.test.ts:45 checks that it contains '!'. Both substrings match almost any render. RunList.test.ts:26-27 asserts markup structure (no '<table', has '<article') instead of behaviour. KpiStrip.test.ts:32 only checks that an em dash character appears somewhere. useRuns.test.ts:13-15 resets fake timers that were never installed. The real timeout path (AbortSignal.timeout at useRuns.ts:42) never runs, because the test fakes an AbortError through the injected `get`. The browser lane does assert real behaviour (RunList.browser.test.ts:49-85), and so do the fetchRuns error-branch tests.

RunDetail.tsx is a 421-line page file. It defines six components inside the page: RunHeader (:92), IterationItem (:155), IterationHistory (:206), RuleRow (:241), RuleBreakdown (:273) and BackToRunsLink (:327). It also holds eight module-level style objects (:29-86). Its markup carries many inline style={{…}} literals, for example at :99-106, :165-173, :180-187, :218-224, :243-255 and :288-295. The return in HomeBody inlines raw

elements with inline style objects (Home.tsx:38, 48, 59, 68, 73) instead of composing named state components. RunDetailBody (RunDetail.tsx:314-322) does read as a short component list, but the page still owns and inlines its own markup and styles.

Loading, error and empty states exist and fail closed: Home.tsx:35-62, RunDetail.tsx:350-392, and useRuns.ts:39-58, which turns parse failures into an error. No partial state exists anywhere. RunsState (useRuns.ts:10-13) has only loading, error and ready. parseRunsFeed (summary.ts:162-167) maps a throwing parseRun (summary.ts:145-156) over every row, so one malformed row turns the whole feed into an error and hides every valid run. That contradicts summary.ts:129-130, which says 'a bad deploy link must not hide an otherwise valid run'. The rule requires a partial state, and no screen defines what renders when some rows are valid and some are not.
